summary: We developed an interactive educational storytelling experience that brings back the stories of two NASA explorers: Sojourner and Ingenuity, whose missions on Mars have ended, but whose discoveries remain essential to space exploration. Through the digital logbook of an interstellar explorer, users embark on an adventure to discover the objectives, history, technological components (hardware), software systems, and major scientific achievements of both machines. The experience offers two interactive exploration paths, allowing users to learn how these devices made it possible to study the Martian surface and achieve the first powered flight on another planet. Our project addresses the challenge through science communication and interactive storytelling, transforming technical information into an accessible and engaging experience. Its importance lies in preserving the legacy of these missions, inspiring scientific curiosity, and bringing new generations closer to engineering, robotics, and space exploration.
details:
Our project consists of an interactive digital educational experience that combines storytelling, scientific research, technology, and creativity to preserve and share the legacy of two NASA explorers on Mars: Sojourner and Ingenuity. Through the logbook of a fictional interstellar explorer who arrives on the Red Planet, users discover records of past Earth missions and become part of an investigation into these two machines, which marked important milestones in space exploration.

The experience is designed as an interactive presentation in Canva, organized through hyperlinks that allow users to freely choose which of the two archives to investigate first. Each exploration path presents the mission's history, objectives, the operation of its physical components (hardware), its computer and programming systems (software), its main discoveries, and the events that marked the end of its operations. At the end of both paths, users find a comparison that helps them understand how two different technologies contributed to exploring the same planet: one by traveling across its surface and the other by exploring its atmosphere through flight.

To develop this project, we used Canva as our main tool for designing and building the interactive experience, along with graphic resources and visual elements. We also used generative artificial intelligence tools to create images that accompany the narrative and represent Martian exploration environments and concepts. In addition, we conducted documentary research based on scientific and technical information about both missions, using official NASA and JPL resources as references to ensure the accuracy of the information presented.

The main benefit of our project is transforming scientific and technological information into an accessible, visual, and engaging experience, especially for young people and students interested in space. We aim to make concepts related to robotics, electronics, programming, engineering, and planetary science easier to understand by showing how hardware and software work together to enable machines to operate and accomplish their objectives in extreme environments. Our expected impact is to spark scientific curiosity, promote interest in STEM fields, and inspire new generations to learn, investigate, and participate in the development of future space technologies.

The creative aspect of our proposal lies in the way we tell science. Instead of presenting technical data through a conventional explanation, we created a narrative adventure in which users gradually discover information, as if they were recovering forgotten files on Mars. The combination of a fictional story, documented scientific information, AI-generated images, and interactive navigation transforms learning into an experience of exploration and discovery.

Throughout the development process, we considered scientific accuracy, the historical importance of both missions, information clarity, accessibility for young audiences, and ease of navigation. We also made sure to distinguish fictional elements from real facts, accurately represent each explorer's technological capabilities, and highlight the value of their scientific contributions. Through this project, we want to demonstrate that although some space missions eventually come to an end, their discoveries, technological advances, and contributions to human knowledge remain and serve as starting points for future explorations.

Because a machine may stop transmitting and a mission may come to an end, but its legacy should never be forgotten.
